column5: Stone Age communities made many of their tools from stone. People hunted, gathered and fished, adapting to different landscapes. Some used caves or rock shelters, while others lived in open-air settlements. The illustration presents a hunter-gatherer camp, not a single dated event. The Stone Age began long before the timeline window shown above.

Flint and other suitable stones could be shaped into cutting edges. Hand axes, blades and scrapers helped people process food and materials. Archaeologists study these artifacts to understand prehistoric technology. Different tool traditions developed in different places and periods, so this panel does not assign all Stone Age tools one date.

Neolithic communities in the Levant practiced farming long before the first large ancient cities. People cultivated crops, kept animals and built settlements. The British Museum's ancient Levant collection covers Neolithic farmers of the eighth millennium BCE. Farming began at different times in different regions.

Cities in southern Mesopotamia grew into important centers of organized life. The region known as Sumer and Akkad in the third millennium BCE developed temples, palaces, craft production and networks of exchange. The illustration shows a reconstructed urban landscape rather than one particular city's appearance at a precise date.

The Indus Valley civilization developed in present-day Pakistan and northwestern India. Its mature urban period included large settlements such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. Planned streets, brick buildings and drainage systems show sophisticated urban organization. This civilization belongs to South Asia's ancient history, long before the Mughal period.

Maya cities flourished during the Classic period in parts of present-day Mexico and Central America. Monumental buildings, carved inscriptions and artworks document their rulers and religious traditions. Maya history extends both before and after this selected period; the end of the Classic period did not mean the disappearance of Maya people.
